import { redirect } from "next/navigation";
import type { Role, User } from "@prisma/client";
import { realUser } from "./auth";

/**
 * Role-based access control for the admin ops portal.
 *
 * The admin surface is divided into logical *areas*. Each area maps to the set
 * of staff roles allowed to see and use it. ADMIN implicitly has every area.
 * The admin layout uses this to (a) let any staff role in and (b) hide nav
 * items a role can't reach; each sensitive page additionally gates itself with
 * `requireArea(...)` so a hand-typed URL is refused too.
 */
export type Area =
  | "overview"
  | "analytics"
  | "clients"
  | "support"
  | "fleet"
  | "billing"
  | "platform";

/** Which roles may access each area. ADMIN is always allowed (see canAccess). */
export const AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]> = {
  overview: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
  analytics: ["ADMIN"],
  clients: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
  support: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
  fleet: ["ADMIN"],
  billing: ["BILLING", "ADMIN"],
  platform: ["ADMIN"],
};

export function canAccess(role: Role, area: Area): boolean {
  return role === "ADMIN" || AREA_ROLES[area].includes(role);
}

/** Any non-customer role that belongs in the ops portal. */
export function isStaff(role: Role): boolean {
  return role === "SUPPORT" || role === "BILLING" || role === "ADMIN";
}

/** Maps admin nav hrefs to their governing area. Unknown routes default to platform (ADMIN-only). */
const HREF_AREA: Record<string, Area> = {
  "/admin": "overview",
  "/admin/analytics": "analytics",
  "/admin/users": "clients",
  "/admin/support": "support",
  "/admin/servers": "fleet",
  "/admin/nodes": "fleet",
  "/admin/ips": "fleet",
  "/admin/provisioning": "fleet",
  "/admin/jobs": "fleet",
  "/admin/monitoring": "fleet",
  "/admin/abuse": "fleet",
  "/admin/infrastructure": "fleet",
  "/admin/subscriptions": "billing",
  "/admin/billing": "billing",
  "/admin/invoices": "billing",
  "/admin/plans": "billing",
  "/admin/coupons": "billing",
  "/admin/game-plans": "billing",
  "/admin/gift-codes": "billing",
  "/admin/email-plans": "billing",
  "/admin/products": "billing",
  "/admin/affiliate": "billing",
  "/admin/testimonials": "platform",
  "/admin/feedback": "support",
  "/admin/chat": "support",
  "/admin/mail": "platform",
  "/admin/orgs": "clients",
  "/admin/visitors": "analytics",
  "/admin/logs": "platform",
  "/admin/newsletter": "platform",
  "/admin/domains": "platform",
  "/admin/grant": "platform",
  "/admin/audit": "platform",
  "/admin/automation": "platform",
  "/admin/settings": "platform",
  "/admin/staff": "platform",
  "/admin/email-templates": "platform",
  "/admin/games": "platform",
  "/admin/blog": "platform",
};

export function areaForHref(href: string): Area {
  return HREF_AREA[href] ?? "platform";
}

export function canAccessHref(role: Role, href: string): boolean {
  return canAccess(role, areaForHref(href));
}

/**
 * Server-side page guard. Redirects to /login if signed out, or back to the
 * overview if the (staff) user's role can't reach this area. Returns the real
 * signed-in user (impersonation is refused elsewhere in the admin layout).
 */
export async function requireArea(area: Area): Promise<User> {
  const user = await realUser();
  if (!user) redirect("/login");
  if (!isStaff(user.role)) redirect("/dashboard");
  if (!canAccess(user.role, area)) redirect("/admin");
  return user;
}

Security section (admin IP allow-list, 2FA enforcement, session length, abuse switches) maps to `platform` (ADMIN-only), enum/range validated, audited at `:303`. No settings write bypasses it — every panel routes through the single `SettingsForm`→`saveSettings.bind(null, section)` path (`/opt/nxeon/components/admin/settings/fields.tsx:25`). CLEAN.

Reset-to-default has a `confirm()` (`EmailTemplateEditor.tsx:183`); bulk approve refuses an unconstrained update (`actions-improvements.ts:80`).

## Defects

**1. Hardcoded status indicators — `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/automation/page.tsx:52, 82, 108, 132**`
All four subsystem health dots are literal constants, not derived from any liveness/health check:
- `:52` `<StatusDot status="online" label="systemd service" />` (provisioning worker)
- `:82` `<StatusDot status="online" label="every 10 min" />` (billing sweep)
- `:108` `<StatusDot status="online" label="worker-managed" />` (port-forward sync)
- `:132` `<StatusDot status="online" label="every 4 hours" />` (improvement agent)

Impact: the page renders green "online" whether or not `nxeon-worker` is actually running — exactly the "all systems operational" faked-status pattern. It is especially misleading because the same page's subtitle asserts `"Every background system actually running on this platform — no vapourware."` (`:44`). The numeric tiles beneath each dot (`jobsDone24h`, `renewals24h`, etc.) ARE real DB counts, which makes the constant dot easy to trust. A dead worker would still show all-green.

## Discrepancy worth surfacing (guard weaker than page area)

**`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-settings.ts:196, 213** — billing-adjacent sections gated below the page's area.**
`const BILLING_SECTIONS = new Set(["billing", "domains", "dedicated-ip"]);` → those sections call `requireArea("billing")`, not `"platform"`. The settings *page* is `requireArea("platform")` (ADMIN-only, `settings/page.tsx:37`), so a BILLING-role staffer cannot open the UI — but the server action is directly invocable, so a BILLING user can still write `domain_markup_percent` (multiplies every domain price), `tax_percent`, `auto_suspend_enabled`, and notably `dunning_terminate_days` — the day a paid-up customer's VM is destroyed. This is documented as intentional (comment at `:194-195`: "BILLING-role staff may thus edit money-facing knobs"), and the values remain range-validated, so it is design-by-intent rather than a hole. Flagging it because the action guard (`billing`) is genuinely weaker than the page area (`platform`) and one of the reachable keys controls VM termination timing — confirm that BILLING staff editing termination-day is the intended trust boundary.

No un-guarded controls, no other faked metrics, no destructive action missing confirmation, no consequential action missing `audit()`.
